en: (13) If impossible—moistened many places, or large part of sack, or threw sack place to place—presumably flour mixed inside:

(14) Rest permitted—where moist flour sticks like dough remains above sieve; flour through sieve holes certainly untouched by water; if yom tov forbidden sift more than need—sift through gentile to destroy chametz; if water fell yom tov and water not in flour mil measure yet—gift to gentile before leavened:

(15) Sifting does not help—even before Passover. Acharonim: specifically sifting not help when dried—but first remedy take moist place helps even dried on Passover if sack not moved and moist place recognizable well as above—rest permitted eat, nevertheless good sift remainder:

(16) For it crumbles, etc.—fine crumbs descend through sieve holes mix with flour; though certainly sixty against them nullified before Passover—on Passover days forbidden smallest amount reawakens; though wet in wet we do not say reawakens as 467:4 and flour in flour is wet in wet—crumbs do not blend well, exist independently—perhaps even at dough kneading not dissolved—on Passover days reawaken and forbid:

(17) Forbidden to eat, etc.—even if baked before Passover—for crumb baked is chametz not nullified as above. See Pri Chadash holds wet in wet does not reawaken—still many Acharonim agree after baking one lump nullified does not reawaken; see Magen Alef wrote further take some flour eat before Passover and hang prohibition on what ate—may rely in loss; nevertheless take other matzot first nights—for not guarded properly—likewise wherever we permit from double doubt:

(18) On Passover—and mice bit sacks: if visible ate flour and moisture dried—some say if on Passover all forbidden—for we attribute mice went many places—mouse saliva leavens like other animals—therefore taking that place not help; before Passover sift and retain or sell as water-moist law. Many Acharonim hold also here taking around bite with flour helps, sift rest, eat Passover—even on Passover; nevertheless good stringent first view except pressure/loss; all when sack unmoved flour not mixed; if shook sack or many bites impossible take and sift—no remedy even lenient view—law like water moistening. Per end previous s.k. even sack moist from water in loss may bake before Passover—here likewise. See Shaarei Teshuvah on this:
(19) Rather sift—to destroy chametz found:

(20) If dried on Passover, etc.—we hold chametz mixed on Passover in smallest amount; if not mixed in time gives taste—if dried on Passover though moisture before Passover—all while moist did not mix—when began mix when dried and crumbled into flour—mixture on Passover in smallest amount—forbidden retain—even if sifted fear small crumbs through sieve holes as above. Unlike dried before Passover—we hold gives taste in all flour, here no such measure. Acharonim: whole seif when known moistened from water; if doubt fruit juice—lenient eat on Passover by sifting even dried on Passover—double doubt perhaps fruit juice, if leavening things perhaps nothing mixed from dried moisture; nevertheless if easy find other flour for Passover—l'chatchila do not rely double doubt eat—hide until after Passover; likewise if moistened something disputed fruit juice or water—permit by sifting:

(21) Forbidden to retain—not wrote throw out—for he goes to 467:10; per him may sell to gentile except prohibition value; per Rama custom there burn all—here likewise. Per many Acharonim in great loss may rely Mechaber 467:3 and sell whole sack to gentile except small leavened flour—plain gentile dish before him:
(22) Dew, etc.—all these leaven if stood without occupation for leavening time—not worse than water—for through occupation does not leaven:
(23) And likewise urine—human adult or minor; but animal and other creatures—dispute whether leavens:
(24) And water of mouth, nose, etc.—human or other creatures—for all are offspring of water and are like water:
(25) But blood—and likewise bile does not leaven—like blood and putrid moisture—permitted make dough for healing:

(26) And milk—in Kamma; likewise milk in brine [and fat] even boiling clear or congealed—for only like fruit juice does not leaven; though milk and blood otherwise forbidden—nullified in sixty unlike chametz on Passover in smallest amount:

(27) And human sweat—and animal sweat see above 453:7 and Mishna Berurah there. Excrement human or other creatures does not leaven—if sack moistened from excrement sift flour, discard dough found, rest permitted. Specifically excrement; but urethra discharge and very soft excrement—some say like urine above. Poskim: wheat in animal dung even soft—we do not say leavened from moisture there—for dung does not leaven as above:

(28) Does not leaven—all equal when alone; nevertheless difference: milk [and milk, fat, blood] like fruit juice for all—with water hastens leaven as 462:2 above; human sweat and excrement of creatures—many Acharonim hold never leavens, some stringent also:

(29) Does not come to leaven—continuous drip prevents leavening flour in drip water; even if moisture spreads beyond drip site—through force of continuous drip absorbing drop after drop does not allow leaven all around:

(30) Drip must be continuous, etc.—drops fall consecutively all day—otherwise waits between drops combine to mil measure as 459:2 gloss; some Acharonim explain: when not consecutive drops cannot prevent leavening:
(31) And bake immediately when it stops—do not leave moist flour without occupation—knead and bake immediately as 459:2; l'chatchila; b'dieved forbidden only if waited mil measure after drip stopped:

(32) And if doubtful—d'oraisa doubt—even to retain forbidden. Same law for grain: if drip continuous drop after drop all day no leaven; if not consecutive leavens from water; even drop after drop—when stops must grind immediately:
(33) Forbidden—see Pri Megadim tends forbid all moist flour—for we are not expert what counts drop after drop—see there:

And Taz—even if no saliva visible in remainder, cow has saliva from unspecified; perhaps dried and wiped and leavens; animal saliva leavens like human—mouse saliva too as 453 Taz 2, Magen Avraham 5: hard wheat little saliva does not leaven—see there. Magen Avraham 3: even horse good give little so none remains—Chafetz Chayim 5. Letter 3 there: blood flecks impossible without saliva like chalitzah—when sucking—end; therefore blood flecks worse—fruit juice with water hastens leaven 462:

Permitted—Taz implies reads wall sweat or donkey sweat—Magen Avraham 5 distinguishes stone vs wood wall—Pri Chadash here. 453 Magen Avraham 10: animal sweat b'dieved perhaps does not leaven—Chafetz Chayim there:

It is fitting to mention here Bach implies three kinds: water, fruit juice, and independent derivative like salt 462; chicken droppings are independent like weasel; if water—only mil measure leaven—see Levush similar to chametz rabbinically forbidden; fruit juice with water stiff—see Or Zarua:

What wrote offspring of water like water—above 120:10 offspring of water—if crushed fish eye for Netziv; YD R' Eliezer 193—see there. Question fish fat on Passover—fruit juice like goose fat? Not general rule all offspring leaven—only what Sages explicit; seven liquids—some make fit and receive impurity, do not leaven—see chapter 10 Laws Food Impurity 2: animal urine not water offspring, human urine is—Tosefta; Machshirin chapter 6 mishnah 5 human urine major/minor offspring of water—Rosh: urethra discharge; human excrement does not leaven—see 467. Machshirin chapter 6: zov and semen impure and make fit; Tiberias water not impure not make fit—great questions: cannot learn making fit from leavening; what does not make fit does not leaven; Tiberias certainly leavens—action 325. Tosefta there 5: Tiberias through mother's opening—see there. Sour apples—Magen Avraham 462; Pri Chadash here red vinegar—see there. Woman's milk—Acharonim letter 12 questions milk in brine as fruit juice. Blood and milk in brine fruit juice stringency—not nullified in sixty; or fish blood and human blood where no taste: animal urine Pri Chadash and Chafetz Chayim; and Iyun Hagra letter 4 will explain more:
He should take—Taz: even when taking moist place still must sift rest flour—Magen Avraham 6:

Not—Taz: whenever can take moist place in sack somewhat more—it helps even on Passover even if dried—no smallest amount concern; if impossible—many moist places—if still wet sifting helps, else forbidden. Magen Avraham 8 will explain; 453 letter 2 distinguishes mixed before or after grinding—other Acharonim: flour wet in wet—but crumbs dry in wet forbid on Passover smallest amount—Magen Avraham and Iyunei Yosef there. If mice ate flour—in sack; in barrel perhaps through all flour as Magen Avraham letter 9—explained there. Chicken droppings sift outward—Bach: not fruit juice but independent derivative—throw outward bal teshaktzu; Taz: also not fruit juice—if kneaded and stood less than mil—not forbid as 462 Magen Avraham 1:

And if—Taz: rest flour permitted when no visible moisture—may rely nowadays; sack with little water—this teaches leniency continuous drip at moist place; nowadays not expert what is drop after drop—Pri Chadash. There: left continuous drip found as was—perhaps establish presumption; see Ten Yuchasin on changing presumption—still since still dripping presumably did not stop—nevertheless now beware. Olat Shabbat letter 5: correct forbid all soaked in water even if dripping—matches here:

Chafetz Chayim letter 17: even less than mil—unlike Netziv—see there; Acharonim letter 16—see there. I did not understand Chafetz Chayim initially; Netziv only wrote without interruption lest waits combine as 459:2 gloss. I saw Chafetz Chayim built on reason and truth. Taz 123 pepper: whether waits combine—great one brought proof from drip implies combine drop to drop mil measure—Taz concluded: distinguish full occupation—waits do not combine; light occupation waits do not cancel—proof Pesachim 39b Rava: drop next to drop no wait between—now understand Taz without interruption means before second drop lands first not finished—continuous occupation; if pause between drops combine to mil—unlike great one who permitted—occupation full—proof Rava teaches only light occupation no combine waits; if so our drip needs drop after drop no pause at all; if pause, combine to mil. Chafetz Chayim unlike Netziv as said. Three interpretations in drip—Chafetz Chayim true—students learn slowly:
Magen Avraham s.k. 1 does not leaven—see Magen Avraham to siman 459:

Seif 4: crumbles and mixes forbidden eat on Passover—I ask: why not eat little before Passover and attribute prohibition ate as Magen Avraham 467:4 end and Taz there s.k. 4 and Chok Yaakov 430—and when permitted l'chatchila may do so; Eshel Avraham doubts crumbs in flour whether attribute prohibition ate—see there; here law explicit no attribution—requires study for law:
Seif 6: drip must be continuous without interruption—see Magen Avraham 459 s.k. 4:

Chew. Bach responsa 6: for giving ill to eat and drink—even rabbinic chametz—stringent without danger; if remedy drinking barley beer or other chametz remedies—eat/drink only with danger, known remedy, impossible permissibly without delay as Rama YD 255—and see above 465:
And some stringent. Rokeach wrote: cow has saliva—must burn remainder lest leaven—end—implies even if saliva not visible we concern:
Permitted. Sweat—and like human sweat does not leaven—Rosh view; forbidders Rokeach compares wall sweat to leavening saliva; seif 5 Rama brings human sweat does not leaven:
Take in hand, etc.—implies rest of flour permitted even on Passover; Maharshal wrote must afterward sift as written after:

Sifting does not help—implies; but first remedy take moist place helps even dry—for we remove all doubtful place; Mordechai chapter 21: case before R' Yitzchak of Vienna—sack of flour fell in mud on Passover—shake sack, said sift flour so moisture remains above, discard, rest permitted—only while moist; if dried moisture not helped sifting—for crumbled mixed, nothing remains above—take other flour for Passover, retain this if finds like dough discard, rest keep after Passover—only if dried before Passover may keep until after; on Passover throw all—end. He did not mention taking moist place—for impossible entire sack or large part in mud—no remedy except sifting—said sifting not help when dried lest crumbles through sieve holes; but remedy take moist place—why not help when dried—for removed doubtful place; Maharshal in name of Rosh on this remedy still must sift all remainder—custom—appears mere stringency; proof Tur: little water or snow on grain—scrape top, take bottom—no sifting in grain—sifting Rosh mere stringency since can do so—not forbid without afterward sifting; certainly dried and sifted after removal—not forbidden lest dry fell through sieve; see 453:3 nullification flour in flour. Mice ate flour—take that place well around, sift rest, eat Passover—not worse than water one place—and not stringent even on Passover—for water on flour law includes Passover from outset. Though Maharshal exaggerated 453 unlike here. Tur in name of R' Eliezer Garmiza: sack flour chickens sat, moist from droppings—does not leaven; nevertheless sift flour, throw dough outward, rest permitted—end. Rokeach adds Menachot 69: barley in dung—if for Menachot bring to your pit not chametz prohibition—end; plain why sift and throw outward—for matzah mitzvah and other matzot for yom tov—not proper disgrace; difference if did not sift—no prohibition at all:

And if doubtful, etc.—Beit Yosef in name of Ran: Rosh wrote not continuous drip forbidden—even what we do not see soaked in water—for flour absorbs moisture and law as soaked—end; if continuous drip permitted others not soaked—Ran concludes unclear. Appears he disputes both: continuous drip permits even soaked—as Rosh and Tur bake immediately; if not continuous drip forbidden only that place—not this absorption concern:
